items.title: Governance locks bring Super Validator and Featured App locking enforcement on-chain under CIP-0127
items.content_text:
Canton Signal Feed (Nov 14, 2026 · 9:12 AM ET)
- **Governance locks bring Super Validator and Featured App locking enforcement on-chain under CIP-0127** — The Canton documentation now details how governance locks will work from Splice 0.10.0: CIP-0105 requires Super Validators to lock a percentage of their aggregate lifetime rewards to keep their weight, CIP-0116 requires each Featured App provider to lock a minimum amount of Canton Coin to gain and keep featured status, and CIP-0127 is the functional specification that moves enforcement of both onto the ledger itself; every lock must hold at least 10,000 CC, Super Validator locks vest over 365.25 days after an unlock while Featured App locks vest over 60 days, and wallet providers have been asked to expand memo fields to 1,000 characters because lock data is encoded in the transfer memo in compatibility mode (Canton Network Docs)
- **SBI Holdings and Cambodia's central bank plan a tokenized government-bond trial on Canton** — SBI Holdings and the National Bank of Cambodia signed a memorandum of understanding on November 13 for a proof of concept in tokenized Cambodian government bonds, with Canton planned as the network and the aim of making bond investment accessible in smaller amounts through local financial institutions; the central bank will register and manage bondholder information, SBI Bank (Cambodia) will work on technical verification of tokenization and transfers, and SBI Digital Practice will build and operate the trial environment, with interim results and a demonstration planned for the Black Swan Summit in Phnom Penh on November 15–16, and a separate memorandum the same day covers a Japan–Cambodia remittance proof of concept; the bond work is a planned trial, not a live issuance (CantonNews)
- **CapConnect+ seeks a Super Validator role under CIP-0131 to settle commercial paper and its cash payment together on Canton** — The proposal, in a vote that opened November 10 with Tradeweb as sponsor and MPCH as endorser, offers a maximum of five reward weight units tied to delivery and adoption milestones, starting with at least $100 million in aggregate commercial-paper issuance settling both the asset and the cash on Canton within six months of approval, then cumulative milestones at $1 billion, $5 billion and $10 billion; the existing CapConnect+ platform, developed in collaboration with Walmart, has facilitated more than $46.11 billion in issuance since full production began in early 2025 on existing settlement infrastructure, which is not Canton volume, and the public document does not identify the anchor issuer for the first Canton transactions (CantonNews)
- **Canton Foundation launches an official Daml 3 developer certification, with free self-paced courses and a $150 exam** — The Canton Developer Certification, launched November 10, pairs free self-paced courses with a certification exam costing $150 per session and is based on Daml 3 and Canton 3.x, the current network stack; it validates practical mastery of Daml's authorization and privacy principles — controlling who may act on a contract and who may access its terms — and gives existing Daml 2 developers a migration path onto the single current platform, with Foundation chief operating officer Amanda Martin framing it as a common professional standard for building in regulated markets (HTX)
- **Canton Coin spot prices widen to 9.06% apart across exchanges, with only a thin best route after fees** — A November 14, 14:02 UTC scan found Canton Coin cheapest on MEXC at $0.07571 and dearest on Bitstamp at $0.082569 across 12 exchanges with a liquid spot market, wider than the 8.19% spread recorded earlier today; the best spot route, buying on Bybit and selling on Kraken, paid only 0.11% after taker fees, about $1.05 on $1,000 at the best book prices, with the transfer status between the exchanges unknown, the best futures route, long WhiteBIT perpetuals against short Lighter perpetuals, paid 0.73% after fees, and no route with a confirmed open transfer was worth taking (ArbitrageGap)

- **Governance locks bring Super Validator and Featured App locking enforcement on-chain under CIP-0127** — The Canton documentation now details how governance locks will work from Splice 0.10.0: CIP-0105 requires Super Validators to lock a percentage of their aggregate lifetime rewards to keep their weight, CIP-0116 requires each Featured App provider to lock a minimum amount of Canton Coin to gain and keep featured status, and CIP-0127 is the functional specification that moves enforcement of both onto the ledger itself; every lock must hold at least 10,000 CC, Super Validator locks vest over 365.25 days after an unlock while Featured App locks vest over 60 days, and wallet providers have been asked to expand memo fields to 1,000 characters because lock data is encoded in the transfer memo in compatibility mode (Canton Network Docs)
- **SBI Holdings and Cambodia's central bank plan a tokenized government-bond trial on Canton** — SBI Holdings and the National Bank of Cambodia signed a memorandum of understanding on November 13 for a proof of concept in tokenized Cambodian government bonds, with Canton planned as the network and the aim of making bond investment accessible in smaller amounts through local financial institutions; the central bank will register and manage bondholder information, SBI Bank (Cambodia) will work on technical verification of tokenization and transfers, and SBI Digital Practice will build and operate the trial environment, with interim results and a demonstration planned for the Black Swan Summit in Phnom Penh on November 15–16, and a separate memorandum the same day covers a Japan–Cambodia remittance proof of concept; the bond work is a planned trial, not a live issuance (CantonNews)
- **CapConnect+ seeks a Super Validator role under CIP-0131 to settle commercial paper and its cash payment together on Canton** — The proposal, in a vote that opened November 10 with Tradeweb as sponsor and MPCH as endorser, offers a maximum of five reward weight units tied to delivery and adoption milestones, starting with at least $100 million in aggregate commercial-paper issuance settling both the asset and the cash on Canton within six months of approval, then cumulative milestones at $1 billion, $5 billion and $10 billion; the existing CapConnect+ platform, developed in collaboration with Walmart, has facilitated more than $46.11 billion in issuance since full production began in early 2025 on existing settlement infrastructure, which is not Canton volume, and the public document does not identify the anchor issuer for the first Canton transactions (CantonNews)
- **Canton Foundation launches an official Daml 3 developer certification, with free self-paced courses and a $150 exam** — The Canton Developer Certification, launched November 10, pairs free self-paced courses with a certification exam costing $150 per session and is based on Daml 3 and Canton 3.x, the current network stack; it validates practical mastery of Daml's authorization and privacy principles — controlling who may act on a contract and who may access its terms — and gives existing Daml 2 developers a migration path onto the single current platform, with Foundation chief operating officer Amanda Martin framing it as a common professional standard for building in regulated markets (HTX)
- **Canton Coin spot prices widen to 9.06% apart across exchanges, with only a thin best route after fees** — A November 14, 14:02 UTC scan found Canton Coin cheapest on MEXC at $0.07571 and dearest on Bitstamp at $0.082569 across 12 exchanges with a liquid spot market, wider than the 8.19% spread recorded earlier today; the best spot route, buying on Bybit and selling on Kraken, paid only 0.11% after taker fees, about $1.05 on $1,000 at the best book prices, with the transfer status between the exchanges unknown, the best futures route, long WhiteBIT perpetuals against short Lighter perpetuals, paid 0.73% after fees, and no route with a confirmed open transfer was worth taking (ArbitrageGap)

items.title: Canton Coin futures open interest eases further to $38.01 million, with liquidations almost absent
items.content_text:
Canton Signal Feed (Nov 14, 2026 · 8:12 AM ET)
- **Canton Coin futures open interest eases further to $38.01 million, with liquidations almost absent** — Aggregated CC futures open interest has fallen 6.15% over three days to $38.01 million, near the bottom of its 30-day range, while 24-hour liquidations totalled only $14.68K and funding stayed neutral at 0.0054% per eight hours; on Binance, accounts are now 51.8% long and 48.2% short, down from a 30-day average long share of 57.8%, suggesting longs are closing rather than shorts building (CoinStats)
- **Splice 0.10.0 caps Scan and Super Validator endpoints and moves local deployments to Postgres 18** — The release bounds various Scan and SV App endpoints at a maxItems limit of 1,000, with larger requests rejected, sets Postgres 18 as the default for Docker Compose validator, Super Validator and localnet deployments, and binds LocalNet host ports to 127.0.0.1 instead of all interfaces; Canton 3.7 adds protocol version 37, which requires a Logical Synchronizer Upgrade to adopt (Canton Network Docs)
- **Canton's $370.5 billion in represented assets is all Broadridge repo recordkeeping, a review clarifies** — RWA.xyz data as of November 12 counts $370.5 billion of represented real-world assets on Canton, 88.6% of all represented value it tracks, all in Broadridge's Distributed Ledger Repo, while showing no tokens distributed to investor wallets; Broadridge itself reports DLR processed an average of $345 billion a day in repo transactions in October, $7.6 trillion for the month, which is production settlement volume rather than distributed token holdings (Daniil Kozin)

items.title: Canton selected to support a three-state RISE benefits pilot planned for the first quarter of 2027
items.content_text:
Canton Signal Feed (Nov 14, 2026 · 7:12 AM ET)
- **Canton selected to support a three-state RISE benefits pilot planned for the first quarter of 2027** — The pilot would combine public benefit programs into scheduled payments while applying spending rules and limiting data access, demonstrating a use beyond financial markets; it is planned for the first quarter of 2027 but requires federal approval, and the participating states and programs have not been disclosed, so it is a planned pilot rather than confirmed large-scale adoption (CoinMarketCap)
- **Canton Strategic chief flags MEV costs for tokenized stocks, with privacy pitched as a safeguard** — Canton Strategic Holdings chief executive Mark Wendland warned on November 13 that maximum extractable value can create hidden costs when validators prioritize transactions, and said Canton's privacy protections and rules against paid transaction ordering are designed to reduce that exposure; the warning highlights execution quality as a live design concern for tokenized markets, and the report also noted tokenized share trades on Canton completed on November 4 (CoinMarketCap)
- **Rome Protocol's Ostia brings EVM tools to Canton DevNet, in an unaudited test release** — Ostia, an Ethereum-compatible chain from Rome Protocol, began running on Canton's developer test network on October 22, with the report appearing on November 12; it supports wrapped Canton Coin, but the release remains unaudited and experimental and is not evidence of production adoption (CoinMarketCap)
- **The Hub reports 1,000 members on Canton, combining creator content with tradable community tickets** — The Hub says its platform combines creator content, live rooms and tradable community tickets on Canton and has announced 1,000 members; the figure is a milestone reported by the project itself and follows an earlier SprintFAM creator-network partnership, although the posts do not establish how many sign-ups came from that collaboration (CantonNews)

items.title: Console Wallet reports full service restoration after a precautionary suspension
items.content_text:
Canton Signal Feed (Nov 14, 2026 · 6:42 AM ET)
- **Console Wallet reports full service restoration after a precautionary suspension** — Console said in its November 12 update that it was fully operational after a precautionary suspension following suspicious activity the previous week; the restoration is the project's reported status and the short notice does not provide a full incident analysis (CantonNews)
- **Cantex adds optional two-factor authentication for actions that move assets or grant permissions** — The wallet update covers withdrawals, transfers, pre-approvals and bridge transactions, adding another check beyond the initial sign-in that users can choose to apply to those actions (CantonNews)
- **Two Canton development proposals pass their votes, for Python tooling and a protected co-validator** — Obsidian Systems' 1.27 million CC proposal to generate Python classes from compiled Daml packages passed and was merged, including delivery and a year of maintenance, and Financial Privacy Inc.'s 4.59 million CC proposal to build a Canton participant inside a trusted execution environment also passed and was merged, covering DevNet and TestNet development, a reference deployment and maintenance; neither vote establishes a completed production service (CantonNews)
- **Digital Asset has 30 open roles as of November 14, with posted pay from $140,000 to $220,000** — None of the roles are listed as remote and 36% are senior level, with Scala, Kubernetes and Python the most requested skills and the highest posted range, $180,000 to $220,000, for a Principal Product Manager for the Canton Network Ecosystem (Landed Jobs)

items.title: Tritemius expands its iOS wallet through TestFlight, adding Canton assets and two Lightning options
items.content_text:
Canton Signal Feed (Nov 14, 2026 · 6:12 AM ET)
- **Tritemius expands its iOS wallet through TestFlight, adding Canton assets and two Lightning options** — Tritemius Labs says the update, available through TestFlight rather than a confirmed general App Store release, adds support for cETH from onRails, HANDL from HandlPay and Edel's tokenized stock and index products labelled AAPL, MSTR, QQQ and SPY, plus a one-click Lightning option that needs no personal node and a personal-node option where the user runs the node and Tritemius acts as its controller; Lightning remains a separate Bitcoin payment capability alongside Canton asset support and does not settle on Canton (CantonNews)
- **REX-Osprey Canton Coin ETF passes its November 13 effective date with no ticker or trading launch confirmed** — A November 14 update notes the filing reached its post-effective amendment date of November 13, but no ticker or trading launch has been confirmed, and a separate review found no post-November 13 filing, exchange listing application or issuer statement confirming trading; the fund, a series of ETF Opportunities Trust, seeks 1x the performance of Canton Coin and would invest at least 80% of net assets in CC exposure, so effectiveness alone is not a market debut (CoinStats)
- **Memora says SOLx minting stops if its SOL reserve check fails, using RedStone CAPS on Canton** — Memora says each SOLx should be backed one-for-one by SOL held in reserve on Solana and that it is using RedStone CAPS to check the reserve on Canton before minting, with minting stopping if reserve data is unavailable or the figures do not match; the November 11 explanation describes the proposed safeguard, not a live bridge launch or independently verified reserves (CantonNews)
- **Cauri Wallet now charges network fees in Canton Coin on sends, a cost it previously covered** — From November 11, Cauri began requiring users to pay network fees in CC on sends; the change shifts a cost the wallet previously absorbed onto the sender, and it applies as a network-fee rule rather than a change to the asset being sent (CoinStats)

items.title: Edel reports a theft of about $300,000 in EDEL tokens, with the stolen tokens since sold or blocked
items.content_text:
Canton Signal Feed (Nov 14, 2026 · 5:42 AM ET)
- **Edel reports a theft of about $300,000 in EDEL tokens, with the stolen tokens since sold or blocked** — Edel reported the theft on November 12 and said it was working with authorities and exchanges to investigate; in a follow-up that day it said all the stolen tokens had either been sold or blocked by exchanges and promised a detailed post-mortem, without giving a breakdown between the two outcomes, and the notices do not identify the affected wallets or establish that Canton's network or Edel's other products were compromised (CantonNews)
- **Canton 3.7.3 maintenance release fixes a sequencer resource leak and tightens party replication checks** — The November 12 release addresses a resource leak that could increase sequencer CPU and memory use over several days and tightens checks around party replication, the process of bringing a participant's contract data onto another node; operators should read the upgrade notes before applying it, as changes affect experimental traffic top-ups, replication rules and monitoring labels, and publication of the release does not mean every MainNet operator has upgraded (CantonNews)
- **Canton Coin burns offset only about half of recent issuance, at 439.3 million burned against 798.9 million scheduled over 30 days** — A holder analysis summarised by CoinMarketCap puts the latest 30-day burn at 439.3 million CC against 798.9 million CC scheduled for issuance, and argues institutional usage must translate into fee-paying activity to improve the token's outlook; the author disclosed holding CC (CoinMarketCap)
- **Progmat's scale in Japan's security-token market underpins its tokenized government bond build on Canton** — Progmat, which signed a memorandum of understanding with Digital Asset announced November 10 to build tokenized Japanese government bonds, already handles 51 of Japan's 103 publicly disclosed security-token projects, about ¥290.6 billion of roughly ¥470.3 billion issued; four MUFG group entities will test bond-for-cash settlement and the full repo lifecycle in live testing this month, the first phase connects Progmat's issuance platform to Canton and to Japan's book-entry transfer register, and 24/7 programmable settlement remains a project target, not a finished product (Genfinity)

items.title: Canton Coin futures open interest eases to $38.42 million as liquidations stay almost entirely on the long side
items.content_text:
Canton Signal Feed (Nov 14, 2026 · 5:12 AM ET)
- **Canton Coin futures open interest eases to $38.42 million as liquidations stay almost entirely on the long side** — Aggregated CC perpetual open interest stands at $38.42 million, down 2.19% over the past 24 hours, with futures volume of $17.66 million running at about 2.3 times spot volume of $7.52 million; tracked liquidations totalled $51.33K, of which $51.12K were longs and only $210 were shorts, and the open-interest-weighted funding rate sits at 0.0018%, below the 0.01% baseline (CoinGlass)
- **Tokenization is measured in movement, Digital Asset's Yuval Rooz tells The Capital Summit 2026 in Korea** — Rooz argued that asset velocity and real usage are the metrics that matter for onchain finance, contrasting them with stablecoin velocity today, which he said comes mostly from crypto trading; the remarks were published on November 14 as a Canton Network update from the summit (CantonNews)
- **FiveNorth recaps CIP-0129: MainNet is the whole Canton economy, with every synchronizer burning on one model** — The recap, published November 14 with co-authors from the proposal, says dedicated synchronizers need no licence and applications need no changes under the universal-burn model, with first users expected in the first quarter of 2027; the recap describes the approved framework, not a live launch (CantonNews)
- **No Canton Coin arbitrage route is worth taking this morning, with spot prices now 8.19% apart across exchanges** — A November 14, 09:33 UTC scan found no CC route in profit after taker fees without a caveat: CC was cheapest on MEXC at $0.078634 and dearest on Bitstamp at $0.085076 across 12 exchanges with a liquid spot market, the widest flagged spot pair is marked suspect, and the best futures route, long WhiteBIT perpetuals against short Hyperliquid perpetuals, pays only 0.68% after fees, about $6.79 on $1,000 at the best book prices (ArbitrageGap)

items.title: Circle Internet Group and Upflam are named in the latest MainNet validator allocation notice as the onboarding queue keeps widening
items.content_text:
Canton Signal Feed (Nov 14, 2026 · 4:42 AM ET)
- **Circle Internet Group and Upflam are named in the latest MainNet validator allocation notice as the onboarding queue keeps widening** — The notice, published November 11 under the heading "Validator Allocations - November 9th", names Circle Internet Group and Upflam alongside AUM-Digik, HostDeFi Validator Collective and Noah HQ; an allocation gives an organisation a place in the MainNet onboarding process and does not by itself confirm a running node or a launch date for native USDC on Canton, and a separate approval notice names five more operators — Canborsa, Carbazena, GateKeeper, Initiativ and Talwex — whose uses range from trading and liquidity provision to institutional commodities and corporate-bond markets (CantonNews)
- **Canton's app reward switch is targeted for February 2027, tying Featured App rewards to measured network traffic** — Under CIP-0104, application rewards would link to actual network traffic rather than manually generated activity markers; the February 2027 target remains contingent on Tokenomics Committee approval, so activation is not yet confirmed (CoinMarketCap)
- **Canton's DeFi footprint edges down in locked value even as daily DEX volume rises above $20 million** — DefiLlama's November 14 snapshot puts Canton DeFi total value locked at $11.74 million, down from $11.96 million a day earlier, while 24-hour DEX volume rose to $20.04 million from $19.09 million, keeping on-chain DeFi small against the network's institutional settlement activity (DefiLlama)

items.title: OnePump launches on Canton with 52 markets listed on its launchpad
items.content_text:
Canton Signal Feed (Nov 14, 2026 · 4:12 AM ET)
- **OnePump launches on Canton with 52 markets listed on its launchpad** — OneSwap's memecoin launchpad has moved beyond its waitlist into a working token market: creators launch tokens that trade early on a bonding curve in Canton Coin and graduate into a OneSwap liquidity pool once the required reserve is reached; its public dashboard on November 14 displayed 52 markets and one graduated listing, JOSE, which graduated with 250,000 CC bonded, and creators earn 0.5% of bonding-curve trades and 0.2% after graduation, paid in CC and claimable from 1 CC (CantonNews)
- **Canton Wallet is back online on a more secure validator, with a one-time passkey upgrade at sign-in** — Users are asked to approve the one-time security upgrade with their passkey the next time they sign in; their address and assets stay the same, no fees are charged and nothing is sent as part of the upgrade (CantonNews)
- **Canton processed more than 5.6 million private transactions in one week, staying above 800,000 a day** — Daily volumes held above 800,000 throughout the week and peaked at 888,000 on November 4, with each participating institution able to see only the transaction data it is entitled to see under Canton's privacy model; transaction counts vary by what a source includes, so weekly totals from different sources are not directly comparable (CC Tools)
- **Digital Asset's DA Registry Proof of Transfer API lets users verify a Canton transfer without exposing its details** — The API lets wallet and exchange users independently confirm whether a transfer of a privacy-enabled Canton asset succeeded, failed or is still pending, without exposing confidential transaction data; Bybit has already integrated it, and Digital Asset is urging other wallets and exchanges to follow (CC Space)

items.content_text:
Canton Signal Feed (Nov 13, 2026 · 7:42 PM ET)
- **MEXC's Featured App status is recommended for a pause over Canton Coin locking requirements** — The Tokenomics Committee has recommended pausing MEXC's Featured Application status because it does not meet the Canton Coin locking requirements introduced by CIP-0116, meaning the exchange's party stops earning featured-app rewards until it complies (CC Space)
- **Canton Foundation opens Community Research Grants for original research and educational content** — Content published between November 1 and November 30, 2026 may be considered for the first round, with up to 50,000 CC per month available beginning in November 2026 at the Foundation's discretion; full terms, including eligibility and screening, are expected on or before November 15, and no grant will be made before then (CoinStats)
- **Wells Fargo is awarded three MainNet validator allocations as institutional node uptake continues** — The Canton Foundation Tokenomics Working Group awarded the additional allocations to Wells Fargo alongside Visoty, Cartumi, Winsnip, Winnode and Otoclick, issued in line with current network capacity and health assessments (CC Space)
- **Canton 3.7.0 brings protocol version 37 with new party-hosting states and lower ordering latency** — Released October 29, the version adds v31 topology transactions that give each hosting participant a hosting state for PartyToParticipant mappings instead of the old onboarding flag, supports multiple synchronizers without a feature flag, cuts CantonBFT ordering latency and bounds protocol, topology and ACS commitment collections, with messages over a limit rejected (Canton Network Docs)

Network: CC $0.085744 | Market cap $3.4B (rank 27) | 24h volume $10.9M | Supply 40.05B CC; milestone: total parties on MainNet rose to 946.8K and total transactions reached 603.0M, with about 1.6K validators, 13 Super Validators and 6 active governance proposals (Crypheat for market data; CantonNews for the milestone)
